title: MCP Security: Poisoned Metadata, Routing, and MRTR State
service: PoisonGuard: the descriptor gate in front of an MCP gateway's merged tool catalog, with the lesson's scanner and whole-descriptor pins, a JSON pin manifest shared by the gateway and the review tool, refresh decisions, a paged multi-backend decision stream in NDJSON and policy-path redaction of audit records

parts.lesson_anchor: Pin the whole descriptor (canonical JSON with sort_keys and compact separators, SHA-256; a description hash alone misses schema and annotation changes); Static scanning is a tripwire; Exercise 4 (change inputSchema without changing the description); code/main.py descriptor_digest, scan_description, scan_catalog and SecurityGateway._visible_tools
planted_bugs: scan_catalog passes tool.get('description') without a default, so a tool sent without a description hands None to scan_description and the TypeError surfaces one call down, inside re.search
descriptor_digest hashes only name and description (approved_fields), so an inputSchema or annotation change is no rug pull
canonical_json has no sort_keys, so the same descriptor with its keys in another order reads as a rug pull once the whole descriptor is hashed
scan_description drops re.I, so <SYSTEM> and IGNORE Previous Instructions get through; the test first sees issues.search in visible_tools, two calls above the bug
visible_tools calls scan_catalog once per tool, O(n^2) digests and scans
parts.timing_assert: visible_tools on 25 servers x 20 tools under 0.06 s. At load average 6 to 12: quadratic version 1.17-1.87 s over 40 runs (2.0-2.7 s at load 20-25), fixed version 2.2-4.3 ms over 150 runs
parts.overfix_guard: exact digest of a stored pin for a descriptor with umlauts, German quotes and an unsorted required list (catches ensure_ascii=False, hash(), sorting lists); an annotation-only change is a rug pull (catches hashing name, description and inputSchema only); nested key order (catches sorting top-level keys only); a description-less tool's schema change is a rug pull (catches skipping tools without a description); a descriptor changed in place after a scan (catches a digest cache keyed by id); shadowing hides nothing (catches hiding both colliding tools); canonical JSON with sorted keys but default separators (exact digest); an unapproved tool hidden like any other finding (catches hiding only poisoning and rug pulls)

parts.lesson_anchor: Store the digest under a qualified key such as notes.export, together with publisher evidence and approval time; Same key, different digest: quarantine as a rug pull until re-approved; Review every new or changed descriptor before updating its digest
parts.exactness: pins read back equal after a reopen: approval and quarantine times with 250, 999999 and 1 microseconds at +05:30, UTC and -07:00, compared as instants; digests normalized to lowercase; publisher evidence with non-ASCII text

parts.lesson_anchor: On every refresh (unknown key: quarantine until review; same key, different digest: quarantine as a rug pull until re-approved; duplicate unqualified name: deterministic namespacing; scanner hit: block and review the complete descriptor); Hash equality proves stability, not safety; Namespace before merging (the qualified name is the public gateway name; never let discovery order decide); attack surface 7, supply-chain identity confusion

parts.lesson_anchor: On every refresh rules applied per backend as listings arrive; Namespace before merging (arrival order must not decide); Use It: a cached approval must be invalidated when the descriptor changes
parts.wire_format: NDJSON: the chunks joined end with a newline and split on \n into one JSON object per line, {backend, listing, key, decision}; chunks may hold any number of whole lines

deviations: Part 1: the quadratic step is visible_tools calling scan_catalog per tool (the lesson's _visible_tools with the scan moved into the loop), timed on 500 tools. The suggested scan_catalog recomputing the approved manifest for 5,000 tools would take minutes; 500 tools keep the slow version near 1.2 s with margins of about 19x and 14x on the two sides of the limit. A fifth bug, the missing-description None, gives the required error one call away from its cause.

Part 2: no simulated crash in the middle of a write. Chapter 13 already tests that trap in 04 (os.replace raising) and 13 (a leftover .tmp file), and a trap class may appear at most twice per chapter. The reference still writes a temporary file and os.replace, and the interviewer asks about it. In its place the manifest is shared by two processes (a stale in-memory copy loses an update), a torn or empty manifest must raise ValueError instead of reading as empty, and the quarantine state is part of the record: the first quarantine time is kept and re-approval clears it, which is the lesson's 'until re-approved'.

Part 3: Gateway.refresh, which records rug pulls on the pins and never pins a new tool, is part of the work, so no-TOFU and 'until re-approved' are tested end to end against the Part 2 store. The scan covers every string in the descriptor, following 'descriptions and annotations are untrusted' and 'review the complete descriptor'. Namespacing is reported as shadowed while every tool always goes by server.tool ('the qualified name is the public gateway name'); a verbatim copy on another server is not approved by its matching digest, from attack surface 7.

Part 4: pages carry an explicit last flag and a listing number instead of cursors, because the lesson does not describe tools/list pagination fields. A newer listing of the same backend replaces an older incomplete one and late pages of the old one are ignored; this is the refresh-after-change situation of the suggested design. Cross-backend duplicate names are tested as arrival-order independence of the event set.

Part 5: digests are HMAC-SHA256 under an audit key rather than plain SHA-256, since a plain hash of a short secret can be reversed by trying every value. parse_path is given; malformed paths raise ValueError, the outer of two nested paths wins whatever the policy order, and [*] matches lists only.
